item.title: Shamonda virus detected in human for first time in France
item.description:
Eva Korinkova/Reuters A virus that usually affects livestock has been detected in a human for the first time. Authorities in France confirmed that a patient who died at a hospital in Lyon in early October had contracted the Shamonda virus, an insect-borne virus that typically affects cows and was previously considered non-transmissible to humans. Midges spread the disease, and the eastern French region where the patient fell ill had an outbreak among animals during the summer months. Officials believe the immunocompromised patient was being treated for an illness that made him more susceptible to infection. The virus was first detected in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, with the first-ever cases in Europe confirmed in late July. Authorities stress that they have not identified any health risks to the general population following the case. Investigations into whether the virus caused or…

item.title: Why the fate of California’s wealth tax could be decided well after the election
item.description:
The passage of Proposition 13 in 1978 was arguably the most significant political event in California during the last half of the 20th century. While its primary purpose was limiting property tax increases, it also made raising other state and local taxes more difficult. It shifted public school support from local taxpayers to the state, profoundly impacted residential and commercial property markets, and spawned tax limitation campaigns in other states. Prop. 13 also fuels a perpetual debate over how California’s public services should be financed that has spun off other ballot measures. One is Proposition 98 , a 1988 measure that guarantees a certain level of state school support. And in 2020, voters rejected Proposition 15 , which would have eliminated limits on taxing commercial property.
